capabilities: Draw lo-fi wireframes with 82 drag-and-drop widgets, 161 icons, shapes and labelled connecting arrows
Render wireframes inline in notes and on Canvas from an indentation-based wf code block
Transform elements in place, present boards read-only, and copy boards as PNG images
Generate sibling board notes and alternate versions linked to the drawing
Describe screens or convert screenshots into editable wireframes via an optional AI genie
extras: AI features are off by default and need a user-supplied API key stored in plain text in the plugin's data.json; the manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff; support runs through a Discord server and GitHub issues.
motivation: The author argues that lo-fi wireframes keep review focused on structure instead of polish, and that the drawing should live beside the spec, notes and open questions already in Obsidian, in a diffable plain-text file rather than a separate tool behind a login.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to draw wireframes, so the screens that belong next to a spec end up in a separate design tool outside the vault.

relations.evidence: Install BRAT, then add Divyaraj-M/wireframy as a beta plugin.
Bring your own API key — Anthropic (Claude) or Google (Gemini), whichever you already have.

summary: Drag-and-drop lo-fi wireframing editor that stores boards as plain .wire files in the vault, with an inline wf DSL for notes and Canvas.
